reconciliation_approach: F-14 (origin/par/night-F-14, 5f8a129b4, ratified COMPLETE, scoped to assess_health) and F-124 (origin/par/night-F-124, 5f8871bcd, ratified COMPLETE, scoped to assess_career vs assess_marriage/assess_health more broadly) were determined to be GENUINELY OVERLAPPING, not complementary: both touched the exact same lines of registry_bridge.ts against their common ancestor -- DOMAIN_READING_FAMILIES + companion DOMAIN_READING_VARGAS/HOUSES/KARAKA_CODE/KARAKA_LABEL maps (only wealth/career keys existed pre-fix), buildAssessResponse's grounding allow-list (checked the wrong key response['completeness'] instead of response['domain_completeness']/['completeness_directive'], a defect affecting ALL FOUR assess_* tools including the ostensibly-working wealth/career pair), and the assess_marriage/assess_health handlers (neither ever called attachDomainCompleteness or attachDomainReading, unlike assess_career/assess_wealth). Neither branch could be applied on top of the other without conflict on these lines, and a naive concatenation would have duplicated the map declarations. Each branch, however, carried one exclusive, non-overlapping improvement not present in the other: F-14 exclusively fixed attachDomainCompleteness's silent no-op path (no precompiled concept-slice bundle for a domain previously returned with zero disclosure; F-14 made it set domain_completeness_empty_reason instead -- an honest null over a silent absence, per B.10 / CLAUDE.md SS N.7 item 6). F-124 exclusively fixed buildDomainReading's per-varga family-label construction: F-14 widened the domain maps but left the varga-family-adding call sites untouched, which -- since that code still branched only on domain==='wealth' with an else-branch hardcoded to career/marriage-cross-check labels -- would have mislabeled health's D6 family 'Dasamsa -- career/status' and fabricated a nonexistent second varga (padded to a literal 'D1') for health/relationship's single-varga domains; this was verified as a real, reproducible defect in F-14's diff by reading current main's (unmodified-by-F-14) buildDomainReading source. F-124 fixed the call site with per-domain labels (Sasthamsa for health, Navamsa for relationship) and a null-guarded (never fabricated) vargas[1], and additionally added a compile-time exhaustiveness guard (AssessedDomain union type) plus exported the maps for direct unit-test assertions -- both judged net-positive, lower-risk additions worth keeping. RECONCILIATION: took F-124's map/label/type-safety structure as the base (independently verified more correct against current main source) and manually re-implemented F-14's exclusive domain_completeness_empty_reason honest-disclosure fix on top of it, hand-ported into the CURRENT (since-evolved) buildAssessResponse rather than either branch's stale diff -- both branches' merge-bases (51096a655, 7bf1bec1b) were confirmed behind current origin/main (340b358cf) via git merge-base, and current main had independently gained an F-31-era missingSliceDomain judgment_flag mechanism after both branches forked that neither branch's diff accounted for. That flag's own contract test (platform-mcp/src/__tests__/assessment_response_contract.test.ts) asserted the exact silent-blackout behavior (no `reading` field at all for assess_health/assess_marriage) that this reconciled fix supersedes with a strictly more informative disclosure (a populated `reading` digest with honest domain_block_not_served entries, plus the new domain_completeness_empty_reason field) -- verified via tracing normalizeAssessmentPayload's spread-order semantics that this is a superseding improvement and not a regression, then updated the test's first two cases in place to assert the new contract. Did NOT port F-124's buildAssessResponse module-scope-export refactor: current main's buildAssessResponse has substantially evolved since both branches forked (gained normalizeAssessmentPayload, an AssessmentKernel type, and several more nested locally-scoped helper functions all entangled with it) -- hoisting the whole function to module scope now would require pulling multiple additional helpers along with it for no behavioral gain over fixing the actual bug (the wrong allow-list key name) in place, so the lower-risk in-place fix was chosen instead. New reconciled exit test platform-mcp/src/tools/__tests__/assess_domain_reading_depth_parity.test.ts (6 tests: 3 unit-level against the exported maps/attach functions, 3 integration-level through the real MCP handler seam, including a new assertion specifically guarding against F-14's varga-mislabeling defect recurring) supersedes both branches' own exit tests (F-14's assess_domain_reading_parity.test.ts, F-124's F124_domain_reading_wiring.test.ts) -- neither should be re-attempted separately; this PR closes both F-14 and F-124.
